title: Smart Buildings
summary: Campuses and facilities use PI System to bring building management, utility meters and electrical distribution data together. Energy-use intensity (EUI) is the headline KPI, and OSIsoft grouped facilities with data centres as a growth market.
hierarchy:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  C[Campus or Portfolio] --> B[Building]
  B --> F[Floor, Zone or Room]
  F --> S1[AHU]
  F --> S2[VAV]
  B --> S3[Chiller]
  B --> S4[Boiler]
  B --> S5[Meter]
```

templates.name: Building
templates.description: Building element with utility meters and floor area, giving EUI. Illustrative.

calculations.name: Energy-use intensity
calculations.description: Energy per unit floor area per year. UC Davis reported a 46% reduction since 2009.

eventFrames.name: Electrical outage
eventFrames.trigger: Loss of supply on an electrical distribution circuit (UMD reduced outage downtime). Illustrative.

kpis.name: EUI
kpis.definition: Energy-use intensity: energy per unit floor area per year.

kpis.name: HVAC energy expense
kpis.definition: Spend on HVAC energy; UMD reported savings of 30%.

kpis.name: BMS reporting effort
kpis.definition: Effort spent on building management reporting; Pfizer reported a 50% reduction.

pitfalls: Electrical distribution data spread across disparate, isolated systems limits outage response (UMD).
Mixing multi-vendor BMS without a common model makes cross-building benchmarking hard (by analogy with Toyota's plants).
City of Bremen's building story uses AVEVA InTouch and Historian, not PI System; do not cite it as a PI example.
verifyNote: The building AF hierarchy, Building template and outage event frame are inferred; no readable PI World deck with a building AF template was found. The BMS benchmarking pitfall is an analogy, not a building source.
